content.value_statement: AI-generated frontend work can look generic and miss responsive states. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code opinionated UI rules for sharper React and Tailwind outputs.
actual_capabilities: Sets baseline design variance, motion intensity, and visual density for frontend generation.
Guides React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and dependency checks before code generation.
Defines typography, color, layout, card, form, and interaction state rules.
Provides motion and performance guardrails for Framer Motion, GSAP, and Three.js choices.
Lists forbidden generic UI patterns and a final quality checklist.
limitations: It contains prose instructions, not runnable components or scripts.
It cannot enforce rules automatically after generated code is edited.
Some guidance may conflict with an existing design system.
It recommends public placeholder images unless the user provides assets.

use_cases.title: Refine Product Screens
use_cases.description: Use the skill to set layout, typography, motion, and state guidance before implementing a complex product screen.

use_cases.title: Shape Brand Interfaces
use_cases.description: Apply stronger visual direction when creating landing pages, feature sections, or product-led marketing pages.

use_cases.title: Review AI Prototypes
use_cases.description: Use the pre-flight checklist to catch generic layouts, missing states, and weak responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-taste-frontend-v1 for a React interface. Create a [screen type] for [audience]. Use Tailwind. Include loading, empty, and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Redesign a Static Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the skill to redesign this page. Keep the same content. Improve layout, typography, responsive behavior, and interaction states.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Motion System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill with motion intensity above five. Add purposeful Framer Motion interactions. Isolate animated client components and protect performance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complex Dashboard
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this dashboard concept with the skill checklist. Identify generic patterns, weak hierarchy, missing states, and mobile risks. Then propose focused fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a SaaS dashboard for operations managers.
output_examples.output: The response describes an asymmetric dashboard layout, a restrained palette, clear form states, and mobile collapse rules before implementation.

output_examples.input: Improve a product landing page that looks generic.
output_examples.output: The response replaces centered hero defaults with stronger composition, unique typography, specific imagery guidance, and cleaner call-to-action hierarchy.

output_examples.input: Add motion to a feature grid without hurting performance.
output_examples.output: The response suggests isolated animated components, spring-based transitions, memoized loops, and transform-only animation choices.

best_practices: Provide the audience, product domain, stack, and visual constraints before generation.
Share existing brand tokens or component rules when they must override the skill.
Ask for loading, empty, error, and mobile states in the first prompt.
anti_patterns: Requesting a generic landing page without brand, audience, or product context.
Using the skill when a strict corporate design system must control every choice.
Adding perpetual motion to performance-sensitive pages without a clear user benefit.

faq.question: What does this skill help generate?
faq.answer: It guides AI tools toward stronger frontend layouts, styling, motion, and interface states.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: No. It is an instruction skill that guides generated frontend code.

faq.question: Which stacks does it target?
faq.answer: It mainly targets React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and common motion libraries.

faq.question: Can it follow an existing design system?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the system rules first, then ask the model to adapt this guidance.

faq.question: Does it replace design review?
faq.answer: No. It improves first drafts, but teams should still review accessibility and brand fit.

faq.question: Why use the v1 skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a workflow depends on the original instruction style and exact behavior.
